title: Repair and Emergency Service Calls: Invoice Payment, Close-Out and Refund Standard
content:
## Clauses in force

1. **Payments.** Payments on a Repair and Emergency Service Calls invoice are applied to the invoice as a whole.
2. **Close-out.** A call closes on the day its balance reaches $0.00, once every discount and coverage credit the customer is entitled to has been posted.
3. **Day count.** Late-payment days are counted as calendar days with the completion date as day 0.
4. **Pending decisions.** A balance that is owing only because a protection contract claim or a Comfort Club covered repair is still being decided accrues no late-payment charge until the decision is posted.
5. **Overpayments.** When payments exceed what is owed, the balance is negative. The excess is refunded to the method of the payment that created it, naming that payment line. Cash overpayments are refunded by check.
6. **Refund ceiling.** A refund never exceeds the payment it returns.

## Clauses no longer in force

- The former clause that the invoice is due the class's due days after completion, with 0 meaning due on completion, is no longer in force as the basis for when the invoice falls due. It has been superseded by the current terms for payment arrangements and special-order parts.
- The former clause that a late-payment charge was posted only once more than the class's late-payment days had passed since completion with a balance still owing is no longer in force. It has been superseded by the current late-payment charge basis.
- The former clause setting each late-payment charge at the class's monthly percentage of the balance, with its minimum and one further charge for each additional full 30 days, is no longer in force. It has been superseded by the current late-payment charge basis.

## Refund cases (hypothetical payments)

| Payments on the invoice | Balance after posting | Refund |
|---|---|---|
| Card payment of $300.00 on a $260.00 invoice | $40.00 owed to the customer | $40.00 back to that card, naming the card payment line |
| Cash payment of $100.00 on an $80.00 invoice | $20.00 owed to the customer | $20.00 by check, naming the cash payment line |
| Check payment of $25.00 creating a $60.00 credit balance | $60.00 owed to the customer | No more than $25.00 against that payment line |

superseded_clauses: The invoice is due payment_due_days after completion, and 0 means it is due on completion.
A late_payment_charge is posted only once more than late_payment_after_days calendar days have passed since the call was completed with a balance still owing.

Each charge is late_payment_charge_pct_monthly percent of the balance owing on the day it posts, rounded to the cent half up and never less than late_payment_charge_min_usd, and one further charge may post for each additional full 30 days the balance stays unpaid.
